answer: Withdrawals climb a mesa one terrace at a time. A new account may take out only a sparrow-sized sum; each withdrawal it completes, signed by its key, lifts the cap one step, if a week has passed since the last. Two nodes check the chain within an hour when a higher step is requested. Withdrawals crowded into one week knock the account to the bottom, and a copied chain fails its signatures and freezes the account. An honest user climbs in three months of ordinary use; 1,000 fakes each need a full chain of their own, the balance waiting at the top like an opal in stone.
